thread:
deploy-bot: :warning: Alert: embeddings-service p99 latency > 2s and error rate spiking (service: embeddings-api, region: us-west-2). Incident opened 1880003333

sara: seeing it on the dashboards, p50 OK but p95/p99 very noisy. looks correlated with deploy 1880003200 (~12m ago) that touched batching policy.

support_ops: multiple customers reporting timeouts + intermittent 502/503s. example error returned to customer: `HTTP 502 - upstream connection reset`

lee: grabbing logs from the inference pool. I see many long-lived batches waiting for the dynamic-batching timer to fire. batch_size target = 64, but we have lots of low-volume clients causing tiny batches + timer threshold 150ms -> accumulates into spikes.

mike: can we flip the batching policy to prefer max-size over timeout as a quick mitigation? or reduce timer to 30ms? Concerned about regressions to throughput.

jordan: also seeing a small but consistent stream of `vector_dim_mismatch` errors for a subset of requests. different stack: appears when requests with legacy embed schema (dim=1536) hit a model expecting 1024 after routing fallback. routing fallback logic changed in the same deploy.

alex: customer report (ACME Corp): "calls started timing out around 11:40, sometimes 502, sometimes 429. we didn't change anything." They included repro curl: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme..' \n  -d '{"input": ["short text"], "model":"embed-lite-v2"}' 
```

support_ops: logs from front proxy during incident: ```
[11:41:12] upstream error: connection reset by peer
[11:41:17] rate_limited: queue_overflow (embeddings:region=us-west-2)
[11:41:45] router: fallback_route selected: embed-compat-v1 -> model_dim=1024
```

sara: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) set batching timer to 30ms for embeddings pool in us-west-2, 2) pin routing to avoid fallback to 1024 models for requests declaring 1536 dim, 3) temporarily raise grpc connection pool size + eject unhealthy backends. Can we do 1+2 now?

lee: I can push the batching timer tweak (hot config, no deploy). doing that now.

deploy-bot: config-change executed by lee at 1880003480: `embeddings.pool.us-west-2.batch_timeout_ms=30`

mike: rolling an emergency routing pin to prevent dim-mismatches. will set route policy: require explicit model match if client-specified dims present.

jordan: running a quick check on recent requests: ~0.6% contained `model: null` or legacy tag; they were getting auto-routed. Those likely saw fallback and then dim errors. putting a guard to reject ambiguous requests rather than auto-route.

support_ops: after timer change + routing pin customers report drop in timeouts. still seeing occasional 502s during heavy bursts.

lee: increased grpc pool size on the heavyweight inference hosts by +20% and enabled aggressive connection healthcheck. change applied 1880003902.

alex: ACME confirmed fewer errors but still saw 1/200 requests fail around 11:55 with 502. they captured response body: `{ "error":"upstream: connection reset" }`

mike: thinking about root cause: combo of (a) dynamic batching timer too large causing head-of-line waits and variable batch latencies, (b) routing fallback sending mismatched-dim requests to incompatible model variants, and (c) connection pool exhaustion under burst causing resets. all triggered by the same deploy.

samir: agreed. good triage. immediate next steps: 1) keep lower batch_timeout for 24h, 2) enforce strict routing on declared-dim requests, 3) add a graceful reject for ambiguous requests (400 + helpful message), 4) run a brief chaos test on pool sizing. assign owners: lee (batching + pool), mike (routing policy), jordan (reject policy + telemetry), support_ops (customer comms).

support_ops: pinging ACME and top 5 affected customers with status update and workaround (suggested explicit model name + reduced request rate).

sara: capturing the repro steps for postmortem: 
1) use many small concurrent clients sending 1-3 items each to embeddings with model unset or legacy tag. 
2) observe p99 spikes and occasional 502s. 
Repro curl loop: ```bash
for i in {1..500}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -d '{"input":["test $i"], "model":null}' &
done; wait
```

jordan: grabbing request traces to correlate client tokens -> backend model variant -> batch sizes. adding a metric for "batches_waiting_ms" to surface this in Console.

lee: p99 fell from ~2.4s to ~380ms after timer change. errors dropped ~75%. leaving mitigations in place while we prepare rollback plan for the routing code.

mike: schedule a canary rollback of the routing change in the next 2 hours if metrics hold.

samir: documenting incident and owners. we'll do a 1hr postmortem call at 13:30 PDT and a writeup with customer impact. good work all, keep updates here. :white_check_mark:
